partners.diseaseBName: hypermetabolism due to uncoupled mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation 2
partners.mechanism_chain: COQ2 (HGNC:2417) —PRODUCES→ Coenzyme Q10 (CHEBI:17700); Coenzyme Q10 (CHEBI:17700) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0005759); Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0005759) —LEADS_TO→ Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency (MONDO:0011829); ATP5F1B (HGNC:7509) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0005759); Mitochondrial electron transport chain (GO:0005759) —LEADS_TO→ Hypermetabolism due to uncoupled mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation 2 (MONDO:0859302). Loss-of-function mutations in COQ2 impair Coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis, disrupting the mitochondrial electron transport chain and leading to primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in ATP5F1B, a component of ATP synthase, also disrupt the mitochondrial electron transport chain, causing hypermetabolism due to uncoupled oxidative phosphorylation. The mitochondrial electron transport chain serves as the shared convergence point for both disease mechanisms.

partners.mechanism_chain: COQ2 (HGNC:2567) —DISRUPTS→ Coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis (GO:0006733); Coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis (GO:0006733) —DECREASES→ Coenzyme Q10 (CHEBI:17036); Coenzyme Q10 (CHEBI:17036) —DECREASES→ Mitochondrial electron transport chain complex I (GO:0005747); NDUFB8 (HGNC:7640) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial electron transport chain complex I (GO:0005747); Mitochondrial electron transport chain complex I (GO:0005747) —LEADS_TO→ Lactic acidosis (HP:0003175); Mitochondrial electron transport chain complex I (GO:0005747) —LEADS_TO→ Encephalopathy (HP:0001295).
